epic.intent:
## Outcome

Today an orchestrator session loads `skills/orchestrator.md` (~4,800 words) plus delivery standards and CLAUDE.md, about 7,000 words, in full for every run, though most of it is situational (failures, retros, redrafts, folders of repositories, Kanban, recovery). This epic replaces that with **knowledge facts** the server hands out by run state.

- A **fact** is a small Markdown file with frontmatter: `id`, `type`, `title`, `scope` (roles, events, topics, path globs), `priority`, `supersedes`, `anchors`, `provenance`.
- Three **layers**, lowest precedence first:
  1. **built-in**: shipped with the app, versioned with `SKILLS_VERSION` (the generic orchestration process, split out of `skills/orchestrator.md`);
  2. **overall**: a separate git repository the person registers once per machine (pointer stored in the Dark Mechanicus home directory); cross-repo conventions and personal preferences;
  3. **repo**: `<dmDir>/knowledge/` of the folder, travelling with the branch like other portable state.
  A higher layer overrides a lower one by the same `id` or an explicit `supersedes`.
- **Delivery**: state-changing orchestrator commands return a `context` field with the facts for the next step (push), and a new `get_context` command returns facts for an event or topic within a token budget (pull).
- `skills/orchestrator.md` shrinks to a kernel: identity, the always-apply rules, and how to use `context` / `get_context`.

## Out of scope (follow-up epic)

- Write-back: agents proposing facts, retro-proposed facts approved at the checkpoint.
- Stale-anchor detection and review flags (anchors are parsed and stored now, not evaluated).
- Automatic pull/push of the overall knowledge repository (the person syncs it with git; the app shows its status).
- Worker, reviewer, planner and sprint-reporter guides (orchestrator only).

## Assumptions

- A built-in layer is needed in addition to the person's two layers, so the shipped process works for anyone without an overall knowledge repository.
- The repo layer follows the folder's storage mode (`<dmDir>/knowledge`), so in db mode it lives with the other state under the home directory.
- No YAML dependency: frontmatter is a strict, documented subset (scalars and inline lists) validated with zod.
- Token counts are estimates (characters / 4).

## Standards

Only the project's Definition of Done gates acceptance. No tests-first or Fireguard requirement for this epic.

successCriteria.text: Facts in the built-in, overall and repo layers load and merge with repo > overall > built-in precedence, and a malformed fact is reported as a diagnostic without breaking the other facts.
`get_context` with an event or topic returns only facts scoped to it, ranked, within the requested token budget, and lists the omitted facts by id and title.

`start_run`, `claim_ticket`, `accept_attempt`, `reject_attempt`, `fail_attempt`, `record_row_check` and `submit_sprint_report` return a `context` field for an orchestrator session, and every event in the catalog has at least one built-in fact.
`skills/orchestrator.md` is a kernel of at most 800 words, and every rule of the old guide is carried by the kernel or a built-in fact, shown by a section-to-fact mapping in the runbook.
A person can register the overall knowledge repository in the desktop app and see per-layer fact counts, diagnostics and the repository's git status.
The runbook records orchestrator context tokens before and after: the old guide versus the kernel plus the context pushed for each event.

epic.title: Knowledge layers: the orchestrator gets scoped context from per-repo and overall knowledge instead of one monolithic guide

bundle.rationale:
Pain point named by the person: all-or-nothing loading at the orchestrator layer (workers are fine). Chosen: a Dark Mechanicus feature, two person-owned layers (per repo and overall, the overall one a git repo registered per machine) plus a shipped built-in layer so the generic process still ships with the app. Write-back and staleness are a follow-up epic.

Graph (one sprint): fact parser first; selection and loading build on it; get_context joins them; push, the kernel split and the desktop card then run in parallel; the runbook joins push and kernel. Critical path: fact → select → load → get_context → push → runbook.

Why one sprint: the deliverable is the orchestrator actually running from a kernel plus pushed context. The parser, loader and get_context have no user-visible value until the orchestrator uses them, so an interim checkpoint would only review library code. Their accepted results and row checks gate push and the kernel split without an extra human approval.

exitCriteria.text: A fact placed in each layer is returned by `dm call get_context` for its event, with repo > overall > builtin precedence.
Malformed facts surface as diagnostics without breaking loading.
State-changing orchestrator commands return `context` for their event.
`skills/orchestrator.md` is a kernel of at most 800 words with every old rule mapped to the kernel or a built-in fact.
The Knowledge card registers the overall repository and shows layer status.
The runbook records before/after token estimates.

sprints.goal: The orchestrator runs from a kernel prompt plus scoped knowledge: facts load from the built-in, overall and repo layers, state-changing commands push context, get_context pulls it within a budget, and a person registers the overall repository in the app.

acceptanceCriteria.text: In a temp repo, `parseFact` round-trip: a sample fact file from each layer parses, and a malformed one yields a line-numbered diagnostic (unit test output recorded).

With one fact sharing an id across all three layers and one `supersedes` fact, `dm call get_context` returns only the repo-layer winner and the superseding fact, ranked as specified, within a 300-token budget with the rest in `omitted`.
With the overall pointer unset, then pointing at a missing folder, then at a real folder, `get_context` layers report not configured, a diagnostic, and the correct count respectively.
`dm call get_context` with no event or topics returns `invalid_input`, and the MCP tool list for an orchestrator session includes `get_context`.

Driving a scratch epic through the CLI as an orchestrator: start_run, claim_ticket, reject_attempt, a failed record_row_check and submit_sprint_report each return a non-empty `context` for their event; the same claim made by a worker grant returns none (outputs recorded).

`wc -w skills/orchestrator.md` is at most 800, `dm call get_context` returns at least one built-in fact for every catalog event, and the runbook mapping covers every heading of the old guide (diff of headings recorded).
Screenshots of the running app show the Knowledge card unset, then set to a real git folder with branch, ahead/behind, dirty state and per-layer counts, and a refusal for a non-git folder.
The runbook's measurement table values match `get_context` outputs re-run at acceptance within ±5%, and every runbook command runs as written.
`parseFact` returns a typed fact with defaults applied for a valid file and a diagnostic with a line number for each malformed case listed in the Tests section.
`src/core/knowledge/fact.test.ts` covers every case in the Tests section and passes.
No new runtime dependency is added to package.json.

tickets.body:
## Context
Epic intent describes knowledge facts. This ticket defines one fact file and parses it. No loading from disk, no layers, no selection.

## Do
Create `src/core/knowledge/fact.ts` exporting:
- `parseFact(source: string, origin: { layer: 'builtin' | 'overall' | 'repo'; path: string }): { ok: true; fact: KnowledgeFact } | { ok: false; diagnostic: KnowledgeDiagnostic }`
- types `KnowledgeFact`, `KnowledgeDiagnostic` (`{ layer, path, message }`).

File shape: a frontmatter block between `---` lines, then a Markdown body (trimmed, must be non-empty).

Frontmatter is a **strict YAML subset**, no dependency: one `key: value` per line; values are a bare or double-quoted string, an integer, or an inline list `[a, b, "c d"]`; dotted keys for scope (`scope.events: [ticket.claimed]`). Blank lines and `#` comment lines are allowed. Anything else is a diagnostic naming the line number.

Fields, validated with zod after the subset parse:
- `id` (required): `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,79}$`
- `type` (required): `procedure | convention | decision | gotcha | command`
- `title` (required, ≤ 120 chars)
- `scope.roles` (list, default `[orchestrator]`), `scope.events`, `scope.topics`, `scope.paths` (lists, default empty)
- `priority` (int 0–100, default 50)
- `supersedes` (list of ids, default empty), `anchors` (list of strings, default empty; stored only, not evaluated in this epic), `provenance` (string, optional)

The parsed fact also carries `layer`, `path`, `body` and `tokens` (estimate: `Math.ceil((title.length + body.length) / 4)`).

Out of scope: event names are validated later (selection ticket); file I/O.

## Tests
`src/core/knowledge/fact.test.ts`: a full valid fact; defaults applied; quoted strings with commas inside lists; each required field missing; bad id; unknown type; unsupported syntax (nested map, multi-line list) reported with its line number; empty body; missing closing `---`.

## Verify
`npx vitest run src/core/knowledge/fact.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`.

reasoning.rationale: One module, but the frontmatter subset parser has edge cases worth care.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `mergeLayers` applies repo > overall > builtin by id and by `supersedes`, and reports duplicate ids and unknown events as diagnostics.
`selectFacts` returns only role- and event/topic-scoped facts, ranked as specified, never above `budgetTokens`, with the rest listed in `omitted`.
The three test files named in the Tests section pass, including the shuffled-input determinism case.

tickets.body:
## Context
Pure functions over parsed facts (from the fact ticket). No disk access.

## Do
1. `src/core/knowledge/events.ts`: `KNOWLEDGE_EVENTS` as a const array with a one-line description each: `run.started`, `ticket.claimed`, `acceptance.claimed`, `attempt.accepted`, `attempt.rejected`, `attempt.failed`, `row_check.failed`, `sprint.reported`, `checkpoint.approved`, `kanban.claimed`, `run.recovery`. Export the `KnowledgeEvent` type and `isKnowledgeEvent`.
2. `src/core/knowledge/merge.ts`: `mergeLayers(facts: KnowledgeFact[]): { facts; diagnostics }`. Precedence repo > overall > builtin. A higher-layer fact with the same `id` replaces the lower one; `supersedes: [x]` removes `x` from lower **or equal** layers. A duplicate id inside one layer keeps the first by path order and adds a diagnostic. A fact whose `scope.events` names an unknown event keeps loading and adds a diagnostic.
3. `src/core/knowledge/select.ts`: `selectFacts(facts, query): { facts; omitted; usedTokens }` where `query = { role; event?; topics?; paths?; budgetTokens }`.
   - Candidates: role in `scope.roles`, and (event in `scope.events` OR any topic in `scope.topics`). With neither event nor topics, nothing matches.
   - `scope.paths` globs (use `node:path` `matchesGlob` if the Node version supports it, else a minimal `*`/`**` matcher in this file) only **boost** a fact when one of `query.paths` matches; they never exclude.
   - Rank: event match before topic-only match, then path boost, then `priority` desc, then layer (repo, overall, builtin), then `id` asc. Deterministic.
   - Greedy fill within `budgetTokens`; facts that do not fit go to `omitted` as `{ id, title, tokens }`.
   - Default budget constant `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BUDGET = 1500` exported.

## Tests
`events.test.ts` (catalog ids unique, guard works), `merge.test.ts` (same-id override per layer pair, supersedes across and within layers, duplicate id diagnostic, unknown event diagnostic), `select.test.ts` (role filter, event vs topic ranking, path boost, priority tiebreak, budget overflow goes to omitted, determinism with shuffled input).

## Verify
`npx vitest run src/core/knowledge`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`.

reasoning.rationale: Pure functions, but precedence and ranking rules must be exact.

tickets.body:
## Context
Reads facts from disk for one workspace, using `parseFact` and `mergeLayers`.

## Do
1. **Built-in layer**: facts ship in `skills/knowledge/**/*.md` and are bundled with `import.meta.glob(..., { query: '?raw', import: 'default', eager: true })` in `src/core/knowledge/builtin.ts` (same bundling approach as `src/mcp/skills.ts`). Add one placeholder fact `skills/knowledge/orchestrator/kernel-pointer.md` (event `run.started`) so the layer is non-empty; the kernel ticket replaces it. Confirm `electron-vite build` bundles it for `out/main/cli.js`.
2. **Repo layer**: add `knowledgeDir: join(base, 'knowledge')` to `layoutUnder` in `src/core/repo/layout.ts` (and `RepoLayout` in `src/core/repo/types.ts`). Read `**/*.md` under it, recursively; a missing directory is an empty layer. Make sure the directory is **not** gitignored by `.darkmechanicus/.gitignore` handling.
3. **Overall layer**: pointer file `<dmHome>/knowledge.json` = `{ "repository": "<absolute path>" }`, read via the workspace's home dir (`src/core/workspace.ts`, `resolveHomeDir` in `src/core/repo/storageMode.ts`). Facts are `**/*.md` under `<repository>/knowledge/`. Missing pointer = not configured (no diagnostic); pointer to a missing folder = diagnostic. Export `readKnowledgePointer` / `writeKnowledgePointer` (the desktop ticket uses the writer).
4. `src/core/knowledge/load.ts`: `loadKnowledge(workspace): { facts; diagnostics; layers: { builtin: {count}, overall: {configured, path, count}, repo: {path, count} } }`. Read on every call (no cache) so a `git pull` is seen at once. Cap: skip files over 64 KiB with a diagnostic.

Out of scope: any command or tool (next ticket); desktop UI.

## Tests
`load.test.ts` with `src/test/tempRepo.ts`: all three layers present and merged; overall not configured; pointer to missing folder; repo dir missing; malformed fact becomes a diagnostic while others load; oversized file skipped. `layout` test updated for `knowledgeDir` in repo and db mode.

## Verify
`npx vitest run src/core/knowledge src/core/repo`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`.

reasoning.rationale: Touches layout, home-dir config and build bundling across modules.

tickets.body:
## Context
Exposes `loadKnowledge` + `selectFacts` to agents.

## Do
Follow the existing add-a-command path:
1. Schema `getContext` in `src/core/commandSchemas.ts`: `{ event?: KnowledgeEvent, topics?: string[] (≤10), paths?: string[] (≤50), ticketId?: stableId, budgetTokens?: int 200–8000 }`; at least one of `event`/`topics` (refine).
2. When `ticketId` is given, add that ticket's `file` references' locations to `paths`.
3. `CommandApi.getContext` in `src/shared/domain/api.ts`; command spec in a new `src/core/commands/knowledge.ts` registered in `src/core/commands/index.ts`; capability `read` in `src/core/commands/capabilities.ts`.
4. Role is the session's role. Result: `{ facts: [{ id, type, title, layer, body }], omitted, usedTokens, budgetTokens, diagnostics, layers }`.
5. MCP tool `get_context` (kind `read`) in a new `src/mcp/tools/knowledge.ts`, registered in `src/mcp/server.ts`; template: `get_storage_status` in `src/mcp/tools/discovery.ts`. The CLI picks it up from `COMMANDS` automatically.
6. Add one line about `get_context` to `buildInstructions()` in `src/mcp/server.ts`.

## Tests
`src/core/commands/knowledge.test.ts` (event query, topic query, ticketId adds paths, missing event+topics is `invalid_input`, budget respected), `src/mcp/tools/knowledge.test.ts` (tool listed for orchestrator, returns the envelope). Update any snapshot/list tests of tools and commands (`roles.test.ts`, `server.test.ts`).

## Verify
`npx vitest run src/core/commands src/mcp`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run deadcode`.

reasoning.rationale: Follows a documented add-a-command path with a template tool.

tickets.body:
## Context
The push half of delivery. Uses `loadKnowledge` + `selectFacts` with `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BUDGET`.

## Do
Add an optional `context` field (same shape as `get_context`'s result minus `layers`) to the results below, **only when the calling session's role is `orchestrator`**. Attach it in the command layer (`src/core/commands/execution.ts`, `checkpoints.ts`, kanban commands), not inside services, with one shared helper `withKnowledgeContext(ctx, event, query)` in `src/core/knowledge/push.ts`.

| Command | Event |
|---|---|
| `start_run` | `run.started` |
| `claim_ticket` | `acceptance.claimed` for an acceptance node, else `ticket.claimed` (paths from the ticket's file references) |
| `accept_attempt` | `attempt.accepted` |
| `reject_attempt` | `attempt.rejected` |
| `fail_attempt` | `attempt.failed` |
| `record_row_check` | `row_check.failed`, only when the check did not pass |
| `submit_sprint_report` | `sprint.reported` |
| `advance_sprint` | `checkpoint.approved` |
| `claim_kanban_card` | `kanban.claimed` |
| `takeover_run`, `adopt_revision` | `run.recovery` |

Rules: knowledge loading failure must never fail the command (log + omit `context`); the idempotent replay of `claim_ticket` may recompute context; the claim token must never appear in context. Update the result types in `src/shared/domain/api.ts`/views.

## Tests
`src/core/knowledge/push.test.ts` (helper: role gate, loader throwing is swallowed). One test per command row above asserting `context` present for orchestrator and absent for worker, in the existing command test files or a new `src/core/commands/knowledgePush.test.ts`.

## Verify
`npx vitest run src/core/commands src/core/knowledge src/mcp`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`.

reasoning.rationale: Touches many command wrappers and result types; must not change command semantics.

## Context
`skills/orchestrator.md` (~4,800 words) becomes a kernel plus built-in facts in `skills/knowledge/orchestrator/`.

## Do
1. Write the kernel `skills/orchestrator.md` (**≤ 800 words**, keep its first-line description format for `splitSkillSource`): identity and role, "Rules that always apply" verbatim, the loop skeleton in a few lines, and how to use pushed `context` and `get_context` (events and the topic list).
2. Move every other rule into facts (one rule cluster per fact, ≤ ~400 tokens each) scoped to the events in `src/core/knowledge/events.ts`, plus topics for pull-only material: `folders-of-repositories`, `fallback-claim`, `lost-claim-response`, `integration-worktree`, `plan-changes`, `retro-redraft`, `required-leftover`, `record-keeping`, `host-catalog`. Rewording only for splitting; no rule is dropped or changed in meaning. Delete the placeholder `kernel-pointer.md`.
3. Bump `SKILLS_VERSION` in `src/core/version.ts` (minor). Update `src/mcp/skills.test.ts`/`prompts.test.ts` expectations.
4. Write the section-to-fact mapping (old heading → fact ids) into `docs/runbooks/knowledge.md` under a "Orchestrator guide mapping" heading (the runbook ticket extends this file).

## Tests
`src/core/knowledge/builtin.test.ts`: every built-in fact parses with no diagnostic; every `KNOWLEDGE_EVENTS` entry has at least one built-in orchestrator fact; every pushed event's selection fits `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BUDGET` with nothing omitted; the kernel is ≤ 800 words.

## Verify
`npx vitest run src/core/knowledge src/mcp`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`.

reasoning.rationale: Must split a long procedural guide without losing or altering any rule.

tickets.body:
## Context
A person registers the overall knowledge repository once per machine and sees layer health. Agents cannot change the pointer.

## Do
1. Main process: IPC handlers in `src/main/desktop/ipc.ts`/`handlers.ts` (guarded like the others, see `src/main/ipcGuard.ts`):
   - `knowledge:status` for the active folder → `loadKnowledge` layers + diagnostics, plus git status of the overall repository (branch, ahead/behind of upstream, dirty) using the helpers in `src/main/git`.
   - `knowledge:choose-repository` → folder picker; refuse a folder that is not a git work tree; write with `writeKnowledgePointer`. `knowledge:clear-repository` removes the pointer.
2. Renderer: a `KnowledgeCard` on the home screen next to `DefaultAgentCard` (`src/renderer/src/home/`): overall repo path (or "Not set" with a Choose button), branch and ahead/behind/dirty, per-layer fact counts, and a collapsible diagnostics list. Use existing theme tokens and card components.
3. No pull/push buttons (out of scope).

## Tests
Handler tests for status, choose (non-git folder refused), clear. Component test for `KnowledgeCard`: not set, set with counts, diagnostics shown.

## Verify
`npx vitest run src/main/desktop src/renderer/src/home`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and a screenshot of the card in the running app (not set, and set) attached as evidence.

reasoning.rationale: IPC plus a renderer card checked visually.
